text:
DET comes in off a 5-4 home loss to STL, a game the Blues won after trailing by two goals, and the Red Wings are missing Dylan Larkin (suspension), Mason Appleton and Marco Kasper. FLA has won three straight, most recently 5-2 over WPG, but plays without Brad Marchand and Aleksander Barkov. Carter Verhaeghe has moved onto the line with Sam Reinhart and Brady Tkachuk, and Lars Eller is up to 17:11 a night from 12:14. For Detroit, Alex DeBrincat has taken Larkin's spot beside Lucas Raymond and Viktor Arvidsson.

The teams are close on chance quality. At five on five, DET has taken 54% of the expected goals (the quality of shots each side creates) and FLA 55%. Our numbers also say the Red Wings are better than their record: a -2 goal difference on +5.8 expected, with finishing costing them 7.2 goals. The special-teams matchup to watch is Detroit's power play, which creates 0.83 expected goals a game, against a Florida penalty kill allowing 0.89. FLA takes 5.6 penalties a game, which keeps handing out power plays.

In net, projected starter John Gibson (DET) is at -6.2 goals saved above expected this season, though he was +10.1 last year. Projected starter Akira Schmid (FLA) is at +0.3, after -1.1 last season. Raymond's eight points in five games, as CBS Sports noted, and a 66% chance of a point make him our top Detroit watch. Tkachuk has 15 points in 10 games, and Reinhart has the best chance to score for Florida at 36%. Our model has it close to even: 3.03 expected goals for DET and 3.08 for FLA.
